nodes.summary: The state of the algorithm holds a vector $V_q \in \mathbb{N}^P$ for each process $q$, where $P$ is the set of processes, and the timestamps assigned so far, kept in an array for constant-time append and lookup. On an event $e$ of process $p$, the step replaces $V_p$ by the stamp $s$ of $e$ computed from the current state, leaves the other vectors unchanged, and appends $s$ to the timestamps.
nodes.title: One step of the vector clock algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $b$ be positions of events of an execution, and let $p$ be the process of the event at $a$. If the $p$-entry of the vector timestamp of $a$ is at most the $p$-entry of the vector timestamp of $b$, then $a = b$ or $a$ happened before $b$.
nodes.title: Own-entry comparison detects happened-before

nodes.summary: For two events of an execution, `a` happened before `b` exactly when `a`'s timestamp is smaller than `b`'s in the pointwise order.
nodes.title: Vector clocks characterize happened-before

nodes.summary: For every position $j$ of an event of an execution, if $p$ is the process of that event, then the $p$-entry of the vector timestamp of $j$ is at least $1$.
nodes.title: An event's own entry is positive

nodes.summary: For every execution and every natural number $i$, the entry at index $i$ of the array of timestamps built by the vector clock algorithm on the execution equals the $i$-th vector timestamp of the execution, where an index out of range gives the zero vector in both lookups.
nodes.title: Array lookup agrees with the timestamp list

nodes.summary: The state of the vector clock algorithm after an execution is obtained by starting from the state in which every process's vector is $0$ and no timestamps have been assigned, and applying one step of the algorithm to each event of the execution in order.
nodes.title: Running the vector clock algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be the set of processes. Given the current vectors $V_q \in \mathbb{N}^P$ of the processes $q$ and the timestamps $T_0, T_1, \dots$ assigned so far, the vector clock algorithm stamps an event $e$ of process $p$ as follows. Let $m = T_i$ if $e$ receives the message sent by the event at position $i$ and $T_i$ has been assigned, and $m = 0$ otherwise. The stamp of $e$ is the pointwise maximum of $V_p$ and $m$,…
nodes.title: Vector clock stamp of an event

nodes.summary: For every execution and every position $i$ of an event of it, the vector timestamp of $i$ is pointwise at most the vector of that event's process in the state of the vector clock algorithm after the whole execution.
nodes.title: Each process's vector dominates its events' timestamps

nodes.summary: For every execution and every position $j$ of an event $e$ of it, the vector timestamp of $j$ equals the stamp of $e$ computed from the state of the vector clock algorithm after the first $j$ events of the execution.
nodes.title: Timestamps are stamps from the preceding state

nodes.summary: The vector timestamps of an execution are the list of vectors that the vector clock algorithm, run over the execution, assigns to its events, in order.
nodes.title: Vector timestamps of an execution

nodes.summary: In an execution, write $V_i$ for the vector timestamp that the vector clock algorithm gives to the event at position $i$. If the event at position $a$ happened before the event at position $b$, then $V_a(q) \le V_b(q)$ for every process $q$.
nodes.title: Vector timestamps are monotone along happened-before

nodes.summary: In an execution, write $V_i$ for the vector timestamp that the vector clock algorithm gives to the event at position $i$. If the event at position $j$ follows the event at position $i$ by one step of happened-before, then $V_i(q) \le V_j(q)$ for every process $q$.
nodes.title: Vector timestamps are monotone along one step of happened-before

nodes.summary: Run the vector clock algorithm over an execution, starting from all vectors $0$. For every process $p$, the vector held by $p$ at the end is either the zero vector or the vector timestamp of some event of $p$ in the execution.
nodes.title: A process's final vector is zero or one of its timestamps

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
